subject: general
question: Which cell organelle is responsible for releasing energy in the form of ATP, which enables various metabolic functions in an animal cell?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria** are widely known as the **powerhouse of the cell** because they are responsible for producing the energy required for various **metabolic activities**.
 
• They generate energy in the form of **Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP)** molecules through a series of chemical reactions known as **cellular respiration**.
 
• Structurally, a mitochondrion is a **double-membrane-bound** organelle. The **outer membrane** is porous, while the **inner membrane** is deeply folded into structures called **cristae**, which increase the **surface area** for **ATP-generating** chemical reactions.
 
• Mitochondria are unique because they possess their own **DNA (mitochondrial DNA)** and **ribosomes**, allowing them to synthesize some of their own **proteins**. This makes them **semi-autonomous** organelles.
 
• The number of mitochondria in a cell depends on its **metabolic activity**; for example, **muscle cells** contain a significantly higher number of mitochondria to meet high energy demands.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER):**

 
 
• The **Endoplasmic Reticulum** is a large network of membrane-bound tubes and sheets.
 
• It exists in two types: **Rough ER (RER)**, which has **ribosomes** attached to its surface for **protein synthesis**, and **Smooth ER (SER)**, which is involved in **lipid** and **steroid synthesis** and **detoxification** of drugs.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus:**
 
 
• Often called the **brain of the cell**, the **nucleus** contains the cell's **genetic material** in the form of **DNA** or **chromatin**.
 
• It controls all **cellular activities**, including **growth**, **metabolism**, and **reproduction (cell division)**.
 
 
 
• **Lysosome:**
 
 
• **Lysosomes** are known as the **suicide bags** of the cell. They contain powerful **digestive enzymes** (hydrolytic enzymes) capable of breaking down **organic material**.
 
• They help in keeping the cell clean by digesting **foreign materials** like **bacteria** or **worn-out cell organelles**. If a cell is damaged, the lysosome may burst and its enzymes digest the cell itself.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Apparatus:**
 
 
• First described by **Camillo Golgi** in **1898**, this organelle consists of a system of membrane-bound **vesicles** (cisterns) arranged parallel to each other.
 
• Its primary **functions** include the **storage**, **modification**, and **packaging** of products in vesicles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **ATP Significance:** **ATP** is described as the **energy currency** of the cell. The body uses the energy stored in ATP for making new **chemical compounds** and for **mechanical work** like **muscle contraction** and **nerve impulse conduction**.
 
• **Evolutionary Origin:** According to the **Endosymbiotic Theory**, mitochondria are believed to have originated from **free-living bacteria** that entered into a **symbiotic relationship** with early **eukaryotic cells** millions of **years** ago.
 
• **Cellular Respiration:** This process occurs in the **mitochondrial matrix** and inner membrane, involving the **Krebs cycle** and the **Electron Transport Chain (ETC)** to maximize **energy yield** from **glucose**.
 
• **Absence in Prokaryotes:** Mitochondria are **absent** in **prokaryotic cells** such as **bacteria** and **blue-green algae**, where energy production occurs in the **cytoplasm** or across the **plasma membrane**.
